merger_description:
Bupa Health Services Pty Ltd (**Bupa**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Partnered Health Pty Ltd (**Partnered Health**) (the **Acquisition**). Bupa is an Australian subsidiary of the British United Provident Association, an international healthcare company with Australian operations in health insurance, primary care, aged care homes and retirement villages.

Bupa provides a range of services in Australia, including:

* facilities and services to independent general practitioners to enable them to run their general practices,
* facilities and services to independent dentists to enable them to run their dental practices,
* psychology and mental health services under the ‘Mindplace’ brand,
* specific services to the Commonwealth Government in relation to visa medical checks and the health needs of the Australian Defence Force and veterans, and
* optical and hearing services under the ‘Bupa Optical’ brand.

Partnered Health is a national provider of primary care services to individuals, and corporate health and wellbeing services to businesses. In primary care, Partnered Health operates medical centres offering general practice and allied health services. Partnered Health also offers skin checks under the ‘Molescan’ brand, dietetics under the ‘Fuel Your Life’ brand, physiotherapy under the ‘Northcare Physio’ brand and psychology under the ‘New View Psychology’ and ‘NewPsych Psychologists’ brands. In corporate health and wellbeing, Partnered Health offers corporate health services under the ‘JobFit’, ‘Baseline Onsite’ and ‘Australian EAP’ brands.

events.title: Bupa Health Services-Partnered Health - Phase 1 determination

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, publicly available information and information
from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• In each local area where both parties supply facilities and
services to GPs and their patients, the market share
aggregation resulting from the Acquisition is low and there
are effective alternatives available.
• In each local area where both parties provide psychology
services, the market share aggregation resulting from the
Acquisition is low and there are effective alternatives
available.
• In respect of the supply of occupational health services to
employers, the parties are not close competitors and the
merged firm would continue to face competition from
alternative suppliers.
